newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Malaysia consider power plant project.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Malaysia consider power plant project.

text.p: Indonesia and Malaysia are planning to jointly build a coal-fired power plant on Sumatra Island that could be used to supply electricity to peninsular Malaysia, officials said on Thursday.

Malaysia's Energy, Telecommunications and Post Minister Leo Moggie and his Indonesia counterpart Ida Bagus Sudjana said a consortium would be set up and led by Malaysia's state-controlled utilities giant Tenaga Nasional Bhd and Indonesia's state-owned PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN).
They were speaking to reporters after signing a memorandum of understanding to cooperate in the energy sector.
Leo said Indonesia had a big coal deposit in Cerenti, Central Sumatra, and that a coal-fired power plant, possibly with a capacity of 1,200 megawatts (MW), could be built there.
"First, they (Tenaga and PLN) will set up a joint venture company. After that they need time for a feasibility study before deciding on the timetable," Leo said.

He added that electricity from the plant would be supplied to Malaysia either via an undersea cable or via overhead cables strung along a bridge that the two countries have proposed to build between Sumatra and peninsular Malaysia.
"The consortium needs to study this in detail," Leo said.
Sunardi, the president-director of Indonesia's state coal company PT Tambang Batubara Bukit Asam, said the Cerenti coalfield had deposits totalling about 950 million tonnes.
"The deposit is big enough to supply coal to four 600 MW power generators," he said.

Leo said the memorandum would benefit both countries. Under it Malaysia and Indonesia would encourage organisations and companies to cooperate in the development of the energy sector in both countries.
The scope of cooperation includes the development of energy resources, energy policy, planning and regulation, trade in energy, electricity generation and power and gas transmission.
